subject: Contract redlines: IP & product-use entitlements (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@plytech.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed redlines on MSA + Order Form (IP / Training)

Hi Rachel / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — PlyTech is excited about the latency profile on Redwood Dedicated. Our procurement team finished a first pass on the MSA and Order Form and attached annotated redlines (redlines_MSA_annotated.docx) and a short SOW (PlyTech_SOW_v2.pdf). The main asks from legal are below: 

- Output ownership: we need clarity that PlyTech retains sole ownership of customer-generated outputs when they are used in our product (i.e., any content produced by our prompts).
- Training/data use: no training or model improvement may be performed on our data/outputs without explicit opt-in per Order Form; we propose a checkbox-style opt-in exhibit rather than language that allows broad "feedback" use.
- Feedback license: request for a limited, revocable feedback license solely for debugging and safety improvements (non-derivative, time-limited).

We highlighted suggested language in the doc and left comments where our counsel thinks Redwood's current wording is broad. Can we get your internal alignment on these points and a readout of the minimal changes that would resolve procurement's concerns?

Attachments: redlines_MSA_annotated.docx (MS Word, 45KB), PlyTech_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF, 28KB)

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: Proposed redlines on MSA + Order Form (IP / Training)

Hi Elena — thanks for the notes and the annotated redlines. Appreciate the clarity.

Quick internal plan: I will own the commercial tradeoffs back to you; Laura will own legal coordination on the MSA language; Ben (contracts) will handle procurement-level evidence and procurement-only terms.

High-level initial responses:
- Output ownership: we understand the ask. Our standard MSA currently grants customers rights to outputs but also contains language allowing derivative training in narrow opt-in cases. We can propose an Order Form checkbox that defaults to "no training" and a separate exhibit for explicit opt-in.
- Training/data use: agree this should be explicit. Laura — do you see any regulatory or platform-level blockers to an opt-in exhibit that pins training off by default?
- Feedback license: we can accept a narrow, revocable feedback license for safety/debugging, but need to confirm time bounds (we typically ask 6-12 months) and scope (aggregated telemetry vs raw outputs).

Next steps: Laura & Ben, can you review the attached redlines and propose markups or specific counter-language by EOD Thursday? Elena — once we have an agreed counterproposal, shall we schedule a 30-min redlines call early next week to finalize?

Thanks —
Rachel

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-09-09T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed redlines on MSA + Order Form (IP / Training)

Rachel / team — reviewed PlyTech's annotated doc. Key legal notes: 

1) Output ownership: Redwood is comfortable with explicit language confirming PlyTech's ownership of customer-generated outputs used in their products, provided we retain a limited, non-exclusive retention right for operational troubleshooting (log retention for 90 days). Suggested clause: "Customer retains ownership of Outputs; Provider may retain ephemeral copies for operational troubleshooting for up to 90 days, solely to investigate incidents."

2) Training/data use: OK to make training opt-in via Order Form exhibit. Recommend: Order Form Exhibit A: "Training Opt-In" with explicit checkboxes and clear data categories (prompts, outputs, telemetry). If unchecked, no model training or parameter updates will be performed with Customer Data. 

3) Feedback license: we can accept a revocable, non-exclusive license limited to aggregated safety improvements. Proposed: revocable for any reason with 30-day notice and automatic termination upon contract end. Also propose an audit scope narrowness clause (no raw output retention beyond operational troubleshooting).

Risk notes: we should avoid language that prohibits aggregate telemetry usage for product quality monitoring; otherwise we lose crucial SRE/quality signals.

Ben — please review procurement evidence list (SLA, SOC2, incident logs) and confirm if we can attach these to the Order Form as a "Security Appendix" for PlyTech's procurement team.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
